title: Passive Voice: News Headlines and Tact — Quiz 119
content:
## Passive Voice: News Headlines and Tact

Explore passive constructions used for tact and in newspaper headlines.

### Lesson focus

1. I have been ordered not to let anybody in.
2. I have been ordered to direct the late comers to the boss.
3. City trader (was) robbed of Rs. 5 lakhs.

### Understand the pattern

News headlines often omit auxiliary verbs and articles. Restore the missing words when writing a complete sentence. A passive can also soften how an instruction is presented, but it can obscure responsibility if overused.

### Worked answers and explanation

City trader robbed of Rs. 5 lakhs → A city trader was robbed of five lakh rupees. 'I have been ordered not to let anybody in' reports an instruction without identifying the person who gave it. Not to belongs before the infinitive in that reported prohibition.

### Try another

Expand the headline: School library opened yesterday.

### Suggested answer

The school library was opened yesterday. A full past-simple passive needs was opened; the abbreviated headline omits was.
